caption:
From #GUANTÁNAMO to Pentagon @deptofwar 

I’m calling out Pete Hegseth @secwar , former Guantánamo guard and my newly appointed “Secretary of Testosterone,” to a cage fight.

Pete, you spent time inside Guantánamo as a guard.

I spent more around 15 years inside it as a detainee , without charge or trial.

You’ve also called for the execution of detainees.

So let’s step into the cage together.

No Pentagon. No uniforms. No guards.

Just you and me.

Secretary of Testosterone, I’m waiting.

Your move.

#CloseGuantanamo
 
#NeverForgetNeverForgive
video_overlay_text_observed: Burned-in captions throughout ("I'M A FORMER GUANTANAMO DETAINEE"); orange CLOSE GUANTANAMO banner, two printed photos of Hegseth on easels; speaker in an orange jumpsuit and boxing gloves.
audio_content_summary: Mansoor Adayfi, held at Guantanamo as ISN 441 from 2002 to 2016 without charge, challenges Secretary of War Pete Hegseth to a cage fight, citing Hegseth's 2004-05 posting as a Guantanamo guard and his June 2026 statement that detainees should have been executed. Describes forced cell extractions ("six guards, dogs, shield, pepper spray, body armors") against unarmed prisoners.
implied_frame: Framing: the man who ran the camp's guard force now runs the department that holds it, and has called for the prisoners' execution. Verified here: the execution remark (June 10, 2026), Hegseth's 2004-05 guard posting, and Adayfi's dates and never-charged status. Not asserted here: the "15 years" figure (the record is 14 years 5 months), the cell-extraction description (his own first-person account of IRF-team procedure, not independently documented in these sources), and the challenge itself, which is rhetorical.
capture_method: Pristine original media + metadata pulled from Instagram's CDN via yt-dlp; delivery webm derived once (VP9 video copied, audio normalized to -16 LUFS / -1.5 dBTP off the source AAC — no re-recording, no in-place re-encode).
